flaws.title: reset leaves hasNext() true when startTick == endTick, so the start tick is processed as if it were crossed
flaws.sequence:
1. A one-for-zero swap ends exactly on an initialized tick t. In Uniswap V4 an upward cross leaves the pool tick at t. Alternatively, an attacker adds a position [t - s, t) while the current tick is t. This position is inactive at t and holds only token1, and it gives tick t a large negative liquidityNet.
2. In a later block, the top-of-block one-for-zero swap moves the price but stays inside tick t, so slot0BeforeSwap.tick() == slot0AfterSwap.tick() == t.
3. afterSwap calls _oneForZeroDistributeTax, which calls initUp(start = t, end = t). reset sets currentTick = t and returns early. hasNext checks currentTick <= endTick, so it returns true.
4. CompensationPriceFinder.getOneForZero calls getNext, which returns t. It then calls liquidity.add(liquidityNet(t)). Tick t's net liquidity is already part of the active liquidity at t, so it is counted twice. If the net is negative and larger than the active liquidity, add() underflows and the swap reverts.
5. If it does not revert, ticks.reset(t) is called again and _oneForZeroCreditRewards repeats the same steps. It computes a range reward over the reversed interval [price(t), currentPrice]. It adds cumulativeGrowth to rewardGrowthOutsideX128[t] even though tick t was never crossed. It then distributes the remaining tax using the wrong liquidity.
flaws.impact: An attacker can make every non-crossing top-of-block one-for-zero swap revert, which blocks those swaps. When the net is positive, the double-counted liquidity skews per-liquidity reward growth. In all cases rewardGrowthOutsideX128[t] is corrupted, so LPs whose positions use tick t get the wrong reward amounts.

requirement_breaks: When startTick equals self.endTick, reset returns early but leaves currentTick at endTick, so hasNext returns true instead of false (requirement 6).
